values.value: Before you start, one thing about how we will read your answers. Nothing is instrumented on either end of this move: no connector reads HubSpot and no adapter writes Marketing Cloud Next. Everything you tell us is your description of the estate, structured against what we know about the target. We treat every count as illustrative until a working session confirms it — the structural gaps we name in your readout are the part that does not depend on the counts being right.

Most of what it backs is HubSpot CMS, and whether any of that is in this migration is the cms_scope_expectation probe rather than an assumption this callout makes: if HubSpot CMS is being kept, this is a boundary to record; if it is expected to move, or if an EMAIL renders from a HubDB query, it is a blocker.","workaround":"Read the cms_scope_expectation answer before pricing any of this. If HubSpot CMS is being kept, record the boundary, confirm no marketing email queries HubDB, and stop. If the content is expected to move: there is no like-for-like target. Each HubDB-backed page becomes either a Salesforce custom object rendered through an Experience Cloud page or LWC, or a static rebuild if the table is small and slow-moving. This is an application-development scope item, not a content-migration one, and it should be priced as such.","manual_steps":["Read the cms_scope_expectation answer first: is HubSpot CMS kept, moved, or moved as a separate programme?","Confirm separately whether any marketing email renders from a HubDB query \u2014 that half is in scope whatever happens to the website","If the content stays on HubSpot CMS, write the boundary into the scope document and stop","Inventory HubDB tables and the pages that read them","Classify each as data-backed application vs static content","For each application: model the object and choose Experience Cloud or LWC","Price separately from the marketing migration and name the owner"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"workflow_reenrolment","status":"unsupported","severity":"blocker","category":"flow_control","issue":"Workflows depend on re-enrolment or goal criteria","gloss":"Flow has no re-enrolment element and no goal element; Campaign Flow has no 'No Re-entry' equivalent either","workaround":"Model entry as a segment and track prior entry in a DMO used as a segment exclusion, then express the goal as an exit condition evaluated by a Decision element. Re-enrolment on a changed property becomes a segment that re-qualifies \u2014 which behaves differently at the edges, and those edges need naming before build.","manual_steps":["List every workflow with re-enrolment enabled and record the trigger property","List every workflow with goal criteria and record the goal","For each, decide whether the behaviour is required or historical","Model the required ones as segment + DMO exclusion and confirm edge behaviour with the client"],"verification_required":false},{"pattern":"sequences_out_of_scope","status":"unsupported","severity":"major","category":"scope","issue":"HubSpot Sequences are in use and were not scoped","gloss":"Sequences are Sales Engagement \u2014 a different product surface, a different budget, and usually a different team","workaround":"Decide explicitly whether Sequences are in or out. If in, they map to Sales Engagement / Salesforce cadences and belong to the Sales programme, not this one. If out, name who keeps running them and on what, because they do not survive HubSpot being switched off.","manual_steps":["Ask Sales directly whether Sequences are in use and how many","Get a named owner and a named budget, or a written out-of-scope decision","If in scope, route to the Sales Cloud workstream rather than absorbing it here"],"verification_required":false}]
